title: KV entropy equalizer and batch-aware allocation strategy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Long-running deployments show steady KV cache fragmentation that increases GPU memory pressure and reduces effective cache hit rate. Traditional slab compaction and epochal rewrite runs are expensive in both throughput and tail latency under continuous-batching workloads. This ticket proposes an "entropy equalizer" allocator combined with batch-aware soft-reservations and lightweight access-pattern sampling to reduce fragmentation while keeping tail latency bounded.
technical_approach: High-level idea: maintain a compact, low-overhead occupancy histogram and a short-term entropy score per allocation bank; prefer allocations that reduce per-bank entropy variance. Combine with continuous-batching awareness: when a batch arrives, allocator creates short-lived soft reservations aligned to the batch's expected lifetime and KV residency (inferred from request trace). Use token grouping heuristics to colocate frequently co-accessed KV entries in the same bank. Evictions use an access-probability decay + coaccess penalty to avoid scattering. Components: 1) entropy meter (sampled, SIMD-friendly), 2) bank affinity allocator with local freelists, 3) batch reservation API that exposes expected residency window to allocator, 4) background micro-compaction scheduler that only rewrites entries when predicted net memory gain exceeds estimated service disruption cost. Implementation constraints: keep metadata per-entry <= 8 bytes additional; sampling budget <= 0.1% of tokens; background compaction runs preemptively only when GPU utilization < 65% or during scheduled slack windows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end e2e benchmark: for mixed chat workload (short+long sequences) fragmentation rate (measured as wasted bytes/allocated bytes) reduced by >= 45% at 95th percentile compared to current baseline (runtime-1.22)
2) Effective KV cache hit-rate improvement >= 6% for representative latency-sensitive production workloads
3) No observable tail-latency regression for p99 token generation (<= +5ms) under sustained 75% GPU utilization
4) Metadata overhead per entry <= 8 bytes and sampling CPU cost <= 2% on a typical worker
5) Feature gated rollout with metrics dashboards (occupancy, entropy by bank, compaction events, reservation aborts) available in Console when toggled on
tasks: Design and spec entropy meter data structures and eviction scoring (Asha)
Implement bank affinity allocator with batched reservation API (Liam)
Add lightweight sampling hook into serving runtime to collect coaccess counters (Eng team)
Implement micro-compaction scheduler with cost model and preemption support
Add telemetry & Console dashboards for entropy, bank occupancy, compaction metrics
Benchmark harness: create mixed chat+embedding workload trace and run A/B tests
Rollout plan: canary -> dedicated rollout -> global enable with rollback flag
design_notes:
- Avoid full-slot rewrites during peak traffic; prefer small, targeted relocations.
- Use probabilistic coaccess detection (bloom-ish windowed counters) to nominate colocations.
- Batch-aware reservations are soft: they can be shrunk or scavenged when pressure spikes.
- Metric: entropy defined as normalized per-bank occupancy variance; objective is to minimize variance across banks.
decisions: Will use 4 banks per-GPU to balance parallelism and metadata cost
Metadata per-entry will be a 32-bit hash + 8-bit bank id + 8-bit residency class (total <= 6 bytes after packing)
Sampling strategy: deterministic modulo sampling on token insertion to keep overhead predictable
risks: Mis-tuned entropy threshold could cause oscillations (hot entries moved repeatedly)
Background compaction could interfere with CUDA scheduling or increase jitter if not preemptible
Incorrect coaccess signals may lead to worse fragmentation if colocations are transient
mitigations: Add dampening to relocation decisions (minimum residency time before eligible for move)
Make compaction preemptible and gated by GPU util; require a rolling restart if kernel-level preemption is unavailable
Validate coaccess signals with offline traces before enabling automated relocations; start with a non-migratory advisory mode
telemetry: Expose metrics: bank_entropy, bank_occupancy_pct, reservation_count, reservation_abort_rate, micro_compaction_events, relocation_latency_ms. Tag metrics with model and route for per-customer visibility.
rollout_plan: Feature gated via runtime flag. Phase 1: internal canary on staging fleet for 2 days. Phase 2: 5% production canary for 48h with automated rollback on any compaction-induced error. Phase 3: escalate to 25% then 100% with performance guardrails. Provide emergency kill-switch in operator console.
